contextual.summary: Queen Mary makes standard contextual offers (up to two grades lower) and enhanced contextual offers (up to three grades lower) to Home applicants who meet one of its criteria.
contextual.typicalReduction: Standard contextual offer: up to two grades below the standard A-level offer; enhanced contextual offer: up to three grades below

criteria.detail: Live in an area of disadvantage defined using ACORN (groups M, N, P, Q, R, S or U)
Received free school meals on any day before finishing Key Stage 4 (Year 11)
Your school or college is sponsored by Queen Mary (Drapers' Academy, St Paul's Way Trust School or Royal Greenwich Trust School)
Your GCSE and/or A-level school or college performed below the national average over the last three years — counts only if you also live in an IMD quintile 1 or 2 area
Home postcode in IMD quintile 1 or 2 — counts only together with a below-average-performing school
Care experienced (standard offer); care leavers get the enhanced offer
Estranged (aged 18–24 and not communicating with either parent)
Immigration permission confirming you are a refugee, an asylum seeker, or entered via a Ukraine scheme
Successfully completed Access to Queen Mary or Realising Opportunities (enhanced offer); Bridge the Gap and Pathways to Law count for Medicine/Dentistry and Law only

contextual.rulesText: To be eligible you must meet one of the listed criteria (the school-performance criterion only counts together with an IMD area). Enhanced offers are for care leavers and those who complete a Queen Mary sustained/partnered access scheme. Home fee status only; A-levels, Scottish Highers and IB are eligible.

source.evidence: Our standard contextual offer is up to a two grade reduction from our standard A-level offer

programmes.name: Access to Queen Mary
programmes.summary: An 18-month programme for Year 12 students from under-represented backgrounds, with academic tutoring, UCAS support, campus and online events and a non-residential summer school; completing it can earn an enhanced contextual offer.
programmes.whoCanApply: Year 12 students with Home fee status who have at least five GCSEs at A*–B / 5–9 (including grade 5 in English and Maths), live in Greater London or within a 60-minute commute of the Mile End campus, and meet one priority or two standard widening participation criteria.
programmes.eligibilityDetail: Must meet one priority criterion (care experience or estrangement; disability) or two standard criteria (first in family; free school meals in Years 10–11 or 16–19 Bursary; Gypsy, Roma or Traveller background; home postcode in IMD decile 1–2 or ACORN groups M, N, P, Q, R, S or U; refugee or asylum seeker; attending a Queen Mary sponsored academy; young carer). Oversubscribed places are prioritised by criteria met.
benefits: Enhanced contextual offer at Queen Mary of up to three A-level grades below the standard entry requirement (e.g. BBB including Maths for Economics)
£500 bursary if you study at Queen Mary within two years of completing (for 20 volunteer hours) plus supported entry to the Student Ambassador scheme
programmes.offerReduction: Enhanced contextual offer of up to three A-level grades below the standard entry requirement
programmes.subjects: All subjects (support tailored to your chosen subject area)

programmes.name: Queen Mary Futures (Economics and Finance strand)
programmes.summary: A 4-week after-school programme at the Mile End campus for Year 12 students from under-represented backgrounds, with subject strands including Economics and Finance and Business and Management.
programmes.whoCanApply: Year 12 students at a state-funded UK school or college with Home fee status, at least five GCSEs at 9–5 (including grade 4 in English and Maths), who meet at least one widening participation criterion; the Economics and Finance strand requires A-level Maths.
programmes.eligibilityDetail: Must meet all core requirements and at least one of Queen Mary's widening participation criteria (care experience or estrangement; disability; first in family; free school meals in Years 10–11 or 16–19 Bursary; Gypsy, Roma or Traveller background; IMD decile 1–2 or ACORN M, N, P, Q, R, S or U postcode; refugee or asylum seeker; Queen Mary sponsored academy; young carer).
benefits: Insight into studying Economics and Finance (or Business and Management) at university
programmes.subjects: Economics and Finance; Business and Management (other strands available)

runs.text: Thursdays 5, 12, 19 and 26 November 2026, after school (Humanities and Social Sciences strands), Mile End campus

programmes.name: Queen Mary Futures Online
programmes.summary: An online programme of interactive activities for Year 12 and 13 students to explore university subjects, build skills and plan future study and careers, with a certificate on completion.
programmes.whoCanApply: Mainly Year 12 and 13 students in the UK and overseas (aged 15 or over); others welcome, with priority to Years 12 and 13 if places are limited.
programmes.eligibilityDetail: Designed mainly for students in Years 12 and 13 (or equivalent) in the UK and overseas; must be aged 15 or over.
